logarithm.def: The exponent a base needs to produce a number: $\log_b c = a$ means $b^a = c$ (for $b > 0$, $b \ne 1$, $c > 0$). The common logarithm $\log c$ has base $10$; the natural logarithm $\ln c$ has base $e$.

log-scale.def: A scale on which numbers are placed by their logarithms, so equal distances stand for equal factors (often factors of $10$). It shows values of very different sizes on one axis.
